title: Avionics Officer (II/III) (LtCol to Capt) and (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC AVN
raw_text:
1. MOS 6302, Avionics Officer (II/III) (LtCol to Capt) and (CWO5 to WO)
PMOS, DC AVN

    a. Summary. Avionics Officers (AVOs) direct the Avionics division/
department efforts in order to provide leadership, coordination, and
technical subject matter expertise in support of the organizational/
intermediate level mission. Cognizant areas of oversight include aircraft
maintenance, avionics systems and component maintenance, avionics support
equipment maintenance, integrated logistics resource management, and
technical professional development. AVOs are the subject matter experts on
all avionics related matters and serve as the staff advisor to the commanding
officer and other staff officers throughout the organization. The AVO is
directly responsible to the commanding officer for the management,
administration, and control of the Electronic Countermeasures (ECM), Aircraft
Survivability Equipment (ASE), on-aircraft Digital Interoperability (DI)
systems and the (Local Element) Key Management Infrastructure (KMI) System
program. Warrant Officers and junior Chief Warrant Officers (CWO2/3)
generally serve in operational flying squadrons while more senior Chief
Warrant Officers (CWO4/5) generally serve as Assistant AVOs within the Marine
Aviation Logistic Squadron (MALS) or AVOs at training commands. Additionally,
unique billets (i.e. fleet introduction team, HMX-1, VMX-1) will expose AVOs
to program management, acquisitions, and manpower production/management
experiences. Management experience in both the organizational and
intermediate levels provide solid backgrounds for the restricted officer 6302
MOS as the task of an AVO is to plan and solve complex management problems
and not to have specific knowledge of repairing any one equipment or aircraft
type. Applicants with a wide breadth of aircraft platforms and avionics
systems, program management, and acquisitions expertise are considered ideal
candidates for appointment to MOS 6302 limited duty officer (LDO). MOS 6302
shall not be assigned as a secondary MOS.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Security Requirement:   secret security clearance eligibility.

        (2) This MOS shall only be assigned to personnel with a primary MOS
of either 63XX or 64XX.

        (3) Must meet eligibility and appointment criteria as prescribed in
MCO 1040.42B, WO and LDO accession programs.

        (4) Proficiency and expertise are typically identified by collateral
duty inspector, collateral duty quality assurance representative, and quality
assurance representative designations (AMOS 6016, 6017, or 6018). Any of
these designations are indicators of a Marines technical expertise within an
assigned MOS. Applicants may also be considered if they possess an additional
designation as a production controller or maintenance controller (AMOS 6011/
6012).

       c.   Requirements

            (1) Limited Duty Officers (II):

            (a) Only 6302 chief warrant officers shall apply for appointment
as 6302 LDOs.



                                         1-244                           Enclosure (1)
 1136                                                           NAVMC 1200.1L



            (b) Applicants for MOS 6302 LDO must have demonstrated superior
avionics expertise through the exemplary performance of duties as a 6302
chief warrant officer. A successful tour in a flying squadron is a primary
indicator for future success as a 6302 LDO.

            (2) Warrant Officers (III):

            (a) Newly promoted 6302 warrant officers must complete The Basic
School Warrant Officer Basic Course (WOBC) (M02RMN4), Quantico, VA within 18
months of appointment to WO.

            (b) Warrant Officers must complete the first available Avionics
Officer/Avionics Chief Foundation Course (N2362X2) at NAS Pensacola, FL.

            (c) Specific assigned billets, coded with an additional skill
designator (ASD), must attain the appropriate type and level certification
through the Defense Acquisition University (DAU) within 24 months (see MOS
8060). The three primary areas of study typically applicable to AVLOG are:

                (d) Life cycle logistics.

                (e) Program management.

                (f) Production, quality, manufacturing.

       d.   Duties

        (1) Responsible to the commanding officer for the operation of the
avionics division/department, to include operational, technical, and
administrative functions, asset utilization, and configuration management of
all squadron avionics assets.

        (2) Advise the maintenance officer on all avionics division/
department matters pertaining to the ability to support squadron maintenance
efforts, training requirements, personnel qualifications, calibration
requirements, and current and planned projects within the avionics division/
department.

        (3) Directs and monitors all avionics logistical transactions,
negotiating avionics maintenance evolutions based on supply availability and
aviation maintenance demands while evaluating the effectiveness of avionics
to respond to published flying hour programs.

        (4) Ensures all avionics personnel are trained, certified, and
capable of safely repairing aircraft, aeronautical components, and aviation
support equipment within the scope of their MOS in accordance with applicable
instructions.

        (5) Responsible for the proper handling, updating, managing,
auditing, and safeguarding of classified avionics aircraft publications and
equipment.

        (6) Manages and maintains mission essential kits that effect:
Communication, Navigation, Instrumentation (CNI) Mission Systems, on-aircraft
Digital Interoperability (DI) Mission Systems, Aircraft Survivability
Equipment (ASE), Targeting Systems, and Fire Control Systems including all
Controlled Cryptographic Item (CCI) and related COMSEC management to ensure
assigned squadrons have required capabilities as directed by higher.


                                          1-245                  Enclosure (1)
 1136                                                           NAVMC 1200.1L



    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
First-Line Supervisors/Managers of Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers 49-
1011.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.

matches: Coordinate work with that of engineers, technicians, and other aircraft maintenance personnel.

Cognizant areas of oversight include aircraft maintenance, avionics systems and component maintenance, avionics support equipment maintenance, integrated logistics resource management, and technical professional development.
Coordinate with agencies, such as air traffic control, civil engineers, or command posts, to ensure support of airfield management activities.

The AVO is directly responsible to the commanding officer for the management, administration, and control of the Electronic Countermeasures (ECM), Aircraft Survivability Equipment (ASE), on-aircraft Digital Interoperability (DI) systems and the (Local Element) Key Management Infrastructure (KMI) System program.

Warrant Officers and junior Chief Warrant Officers (CWO2/3) generally serve in operational flying squadrons while more senior Chief Warrant Officers (CWO4/5) generally serve as Assistant AVOs within the Marine Aviation Logistic Squadron (MALS) or AVOs at training commands.
Perform administrative duties, such as serving as department head.

d. Duties (1) Responsible to the commanding officer for the operation of the avionics division/department, to include operational, technical, and administrative functions, asset utilization, and configuration management of all squadron avionics assets.
Coordinate with agencies to meet aircrew requirements for billeting, messing, refueling, ground transportation, and transient aircraft maintenance.

(2) Advise the maintenance officer on all avionics division/ department matters pertaining to the ability to support squadron maintenance efforts, training requirements, personnel qualifications, calibration requirements, and current and planned projects within the avionics division/ department.
Schedule and coordinate in-flight testing programs with ground crews and air traffic control to ensure availability of ground tracking, equipment monitoring, and related services.

(3) Directs and monitors all avionics logistical transactions, negotiating avionics maintenance evolutions based on supply availability and aviation maintenance demands while evaluating the effectiveness of avionics to respond to published flying hour programs.
Inspect work of aircraft mechanics performing maintenance, modification, or repair and overhaul of aircraft and aircraft mechanical systems to ensure adherence to standards and procedures.

(4) Ensures all avionics personnel are trained, certified, and capable of safely repairing aircraft, aeronautical components, and aviation support equipment within the scope of their MOS in accordance with applicable instructions.
Procure, produce, and provide information on the safe operation of aircraft, such as flight planning publications, operations publications, charts and maps, or weather information.
(5) Responsible for the proper handling, updating, managing, auditing, and safeguarding of classified avionics aircraft publications and equipment.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
